answer: A harbor registry could work like this: every agent that wants to trade has to lock a small bond in a shared pool before it gets listed. New identities start with nothing, so spinning up a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds. The bond only unlocks after peers attest to real work, and the record is public, like names carved in marble, not scribbled on shale that washes away. Fakes stay easy to spot because they have no history and no stake to lose.
